newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi unionist says support growing for strike.
newsitem.headline: Malawi unionist says support growing for strike.

text.p: Thirteen public sector unions in Malawi have pledged their support for a strike by the Civil Servants' Union, its leader Thomas Banda said on Monday.

Finance Minister Aleke Banda said 90 percent of the civil service was still functioning in spite of the strike, because employees in the biggest revenue earners -- the customs and income tax departments -- were still working.
He said workers at some state hospitals had joined the strike which was also affecting ambulance and nursing services.
The 100,000 strong union is pushing for a 100-percent wage increase recommended by an independent commission of inquiry. The lowest-paid civil servant earns $20 per month.
Banda said executive members from the Malawi Congress of Trade Unions (MCTU) would begin talks with government soon.
Malawi President Bakili Muluzi said a billion kwacha ($67 million) was needed to implement the commission's proposals, but that the country's economy could not afford the increase.
The government has proposed implementing the raise in phases to avoid destabilising the economy, which is fighting 7.1 percent annual inflation.

The cabinet economic committee chairman Cassim Chilumpha told national radio on Sunday: "Contrary to what is being said, government is committed to implement the recommendations in full. Government is also cautious of some of the recommendations of the report, such as retrenchment."
The government made provision in its budget for the year ending April 1998 for an average 47-percent wage increase for government workers.
